name: Dark romanticism style

lead: Dark romanticism as a style borrows from the literary and artistic movement of the same name, which focused on melancholy, the gothic and strong emotion. In dress it translates to dark colors, textures such as velvet or lace, and historically flavored pieces that create a brooding, poetic image.
It overlaps with goth fashion and the internet aesthetic dark academia. People adopt it to look distinctive and cohesive, using clothing, grooming and makeup choices rather than any treatment.

paras: Wardrobe choices usually include dark or muted palettes, tailored coats, blazers or cardigans, tweed or houndstooth, and sometimes lace or velvet details, paired with dramatic grooming such as dark eyeliner. People assemble looks gradually from thrifted and tailored pieces.
There are no physical risks beyond those of any clothing or cosmetics. The look is aesthetic and context-dependent.

angle.text: The look changes appearance through clothing, color and grooming choices. Its appeal is a coherent, atmospheric image that stands apart from mainstream dress.

lead: Dark romanticism style is an appearance aesthetic drawing on Dark Romanticism, a literary subgenre of Romanticism named by Mario Praz in 1930 that focuses on the irrational, melancholy, madness and the gothic.[1] Its figures include Edgar Allan Poe, and its painting favors dark, enigmatic backdrops.[1]

As a look it sits near gothic fashion, whose roots are traced to Victorian mourning culture and which features black clothing, velvet, lace and dramatic makeup, and near dark academia, an internet aesthetic of tweed, blazers, Oxford shoes and a palette of black, brown and dark green.[2][3]

paras: Dark Romanticism emphasized human imperfection, guilt, melancholia and raw emotion over reason, in reaction to the Enlightenment.[1] Painters such as Goya, Fuseli and Delacroix are named in this tradition.[1]

Gothic fashion is described as predominantly black with velvet, lace and leather, with dark makeup for all genders.[2] Dark academia emerged on Tumblr around 2014 to 2015, centered on Donna Tartt's The Secret History, and spread through Instagram, Pinterest and TikTok, with Romantic-era writers such as Byron and Shelley cited as influences.[3]

timeline.event: Mario Praz names Dark Romanticism in The Romantic Agony.[1]
Dark academia begins to emerge on Tumblr, spreading widely in the early 2020s.[3]
